```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6,
                      fig.height = 4, dpi = 150)
```

`cellprograms` discovers transcriptional programs **de novo within each cell
type** from pseudobulk single-cell RNA-seq, then investigates cross-cell-type
coordination and sharing afterwards — never assuming it. This vignette runs
the whole pipeline on a small simulated dataset.

## Simulate pseudobulk data

`simulate_pseudobulk()` plants private and shared programs with known ground
truth. The result is a named list of observations x genes matrices, one per
cell type.

```{r simulate}
library(cellprograms)

sim <- simulate_pseudobulk(scenario = "mixed", n_samples = 60,
                           n_genes = 800, program_size = 40, seed = 1)
str(sim$pseudobulk, max.level = 1)
```

## Build the data object and fit programs

```{r fit}
x <- as_cell_program_data(sim$pseudobulk)
validate_cell_program_data(x)

fit <- fit_celltype_programs(x, loading_prior = "point_laplace",
                             max_factors = 6, features = "variable",
                             n_variable_genes = 400)
fit <- canonicalize_programs(fit)
fit
```

`fit_celltype_programs()` fits one empirical-Bayes matrix factorization per
cell type ('flashier'); `canonicalize_programs()` resolves sign and scale
ambiguity so programs are comparable downstream. Real-data fits should
additionally pass `covariates` (e.g. `c("site", "sex")`) and use
`max_factors = 30` when the goal is CMP detection (see the CMP benchmark note
in `README`).

## From single cells: metacells (optional)

When the starting point is a single-cell object rather than pseudobulk
profiles, `MetacellsByGroupsSEACells()` aggregates cells into
transcriptomically homogeneous metacells with SEACells (run in an isolated
basilisk-managed Python environment, built on first use) and mcRigor QC,
stratified so metacells never cross donors or cell types. The metacell
counts feed `fit_celltype_programs()` directly:

```{r metacells, eval=FALSE}
# Requires: install.packages("Seurat"); remotes::install_github("JSB-UCLA/mcRigor");
# BiocManager::install("basilisk")
seu <- MetacellsByGroupsSEACells(
  seurat_obj,                         # Seurat object with raw counts + PCA
  group.by = c("donor", "celltype"),  # stratification: metacells stay within donor x cell type
  cells_per_metacell = 75,
  min_cells = 100
)
res <- GetMetacellSEACells(seu)
mc <- res$metacell_object
head(res$qc)  # per-metacell mcRigor QC (mcDiv, dubious flag, ZeroRate)

# Metacell counts -> named list of metacells x genes matrices, one per cell type
counts <- SeuratObject::LayerData(mc[["RNA"]], layer = "counts")  # genes x metacells
by_type <- split(colnames(mc), mc$celltype)
pb <- lapply(by_type, function(cells) t(as.matrix(counts[, cells, drop = FALSE])))

x <- as_cell_program_data(pb)
fit <- fit_celltype_programs(x, loading_prior = "point_laplace",
                             max_factors = 6, features = "variable")
fit <- canonicalize_programs(fit)
```

`OptimizeGammaSEACells()` selects the granularity (`cells_per_metacell`) by
the mcRigor score when you prefer data-driven granularity over the default.

## Inspect programs

```{r inspect}
program_summary(fit)          # one row per cell type: K, R2, ELBO
top_genes(fit, "B_1", n = 8)  # top loadings of program B_1
```

Scores (donor x program activities) and loadings (gene x program) are one call
away:

```{r extract}
Z <- program_scores(fit)    # donors x all programs (wide matrix)
W <- program_loadings(fit)  # genes x all programs
dim(Z); dim(W)
```

The same views as figures — donor x program score heatmap (with the planted
context as an annotation strip), top loadings, and per-program variance
explained:

```{r viz-inspect, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.5}
sev <- sim$truth$B[[1]]$z > median(sim$truth$B[[1]]$z)
md <- data.frame(observation_id = paste0("obs", seq_along(sev)),
                 planted = factor(sev, c(FALSE, TRUE), c("low", "high")))
fit_ann <- as_cell_program_data(sim$pseudobulk, sample_metadata = md)
fit_ann <- canonicalize_programs(fit_celltype_programs(fit_ann, loading_prior = "point_laplace",
                                                       max_factors = 6, features = "variable",
                                                       n_variable_genes = 400))
plot_program_scores(fit_ann, annotation = "planted")
plot_top_genes(fit, c("B_1", "CD4_1"), n = 8)
plot_variance_explained(fit)
```

## Stability

`assess_program_stability()` refits on donor subsamples and reports how often
each program is recovered. Refits that fail are counted, not silently
dropped: `fit$stability` carries `valid_refits`/`failed_refits` and a
per-replicate `replicate_log`; `recovery_freq` keeps its legacy meaning (hits
over requested iterations) while `conditional_recovery_freq` is computed over
successful refits (all refits failing yields `NA`, not 0).

```{r stability}
fit <- assess_program_stability(fit, n_boot = 4, resample_frac = 0.7,
                                seed = 1, progress = FALSE)
fit$stability$per_program
plot_stability(fit)
```

## Coordinated multicellular programs (CMPs)

`find_coordinated_programs()` tests whether programs from *different* cell
types co-vary across donors, with family-wise error control by permutation.
Gene overlap plays no role in the call.

```{r cmp}
cmp <- find_coordinated_programs(fit, n_perm = 199, seed = 1)
cmp
```

The coordination network (node size = pooled evidence A_v, edge width = |T|,
color = CMP membership) and the per-program node statistics:

```{r viz-cmp, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5.5}
plot_cmp_network(cmp)
plot_cmp_nodes(cmp)
```

## Shared vs specific programs

`program_sharing()` goes the other way: it matches programs across cell types
by loading correlation (permutation-calibrated), then asks with 'mashr'
whether the matched programs share their gene *effects* — correlated loadings
alone do not imply shared effects.

```{r sharing}
if (requireNamespace("mashr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  shr <- program_sharing(fit, n_perm = 99, seed = 1)
  shr
  plot_sharing(shr)   # pre-screen correlations x mashr classification
}
```

## Artifact genes

Immunoglobulin/TCR V(D)J segments, known donor-genotype markers, and
sex-chromosome genes can dominate programs for technical or genetic rather
than biological reasons. Flag them in existing fits, or exclude them at fit
time (exclusion happens before variable-gene selection):

```{r viz-artifacts, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
plot_artifact_flags(flag_artifact_genes(fit))
flag_artifact_genes(fit)

# fit-time masking:
# excl <- artifact_genes(colnames(sim$pseudobulk$B))
# fit_masked <- fit_celltype_programs(x, exclude_genes = excl, ...)
```
